title: Shannon Entropy: Measuring Uncertainty
hook: How many bits does it take to describe the outcome of a random experiment? Explore how uncertainty depends on the probabilities.

equation.caption: Entropy of a discrete probability distribution.

explorations.title: Certainty vs. Uncertainty
explorations.predict: What is the entropy when one outcome has probability 1?
explorations.observe: Entropy is 0 bits. The outcome is certain.
explorations.why: When p_i = 1, the term -p_i log2 p_i = 0 because log2(1) = 0. All other terms are 0 because p_i = 0 (and 0 log 0 = 0). Thus H = 0.

explorations.title: Equally Likely Outcomes
explorations.predict: What is the entropy when four outcomes are equally likely?
explorations.why: For uniform distribution with n outcomes, H = log2(n). With n=4, H = log2(4) = 2 bits.

limitation: This interactive assumes a discrete probability distribution with a fixed number of outcomes. It does not cover continuous entropy (differential entropy) or the entropy of sequences with memory.
misconception: Entropy is not the number of outcomes; it is the average uncertainty. A distribution with many outcomes can have low entropy if one outcome is very likely.

claims.text: Entropy is defined as H = -Σ p_i log2 p_i.
For a uniform distribution over n outcomes, H = log2(n).
The toy setup uses a fixed set of up to 4 outcomes and auto-normalizes probabilities to sum to 1.
